note: What this project produces that another project can consume, and what it currently consumes from others. Written so a reader does not have to reverse-engineer the repository to find out. Every 'measured' line is something that was run, with the date; every 'not-consumed' line is a real absence, not a plan.

produces.what: a zip that unpacks into a runner, a verifier and 58 cases
produces.how: curl the raw URL, unpack, `python run.py` in a clean directory
produces.measured: 2026-11-27: 389,203 bytes, sha256 a5c0e5b7...71ffc, 58/58 rc=0 on Windows and on Linux, anonymously fetched on both
produces.caveat: the archive is not byte-identical across operating systems: the same tree built on Linux gives 389,201 bytes / e57c052f...

produces.what: one JSON line per package, written by the verifier itself: vector, result, checks_failed, verifier identity, exit code
produces.where: uibc_core.pyz verify <pkg> --report <file.jsonl> --vector-id <id>, or uibc_core.pyz verify-dir <dir> --report <file.jsonl>; shape: interop/verify-report.schema.json (draft 2020-12); checker: tools/report_lint.py
produces.measured: 2026-11-27: six contracts in tests/test_verify_report.py; on Linux, 58 shipped cases produced 58 lines and 52 of them named the failing check; an unreadable input (a single statement file) produced one ERROR line with exit 3; 2026-11-27 (later): six schema contracts plus an optional jsonschema validation pass
produces.caveat: the line carries our verdict vocabulary and our check ids; a consumer still has to map both. Lines are appended, so a harness must not assume one line per file

produces.what: one JSON object per package: result, checks with ids, and the reason for each
produces.how: run the pyz with a Python 3 interpreter; stdout is the JSON, stderr is the explanation
produces.measured: 2026-11-27: on 58 shipped cases, and on 3 packages built by someone else, the verdict never disagreed with the expectation
produces.caveat: the verdict vocabulary is ours. A consumer expecting a boolean pass/fail has to map FAIL, INCONCLUSIVE and abstention onto its own scale, and that mapping is the consumer's claim, not ours

produces.what: the record a kit run leaves behind: verifier version, case count, passed count, and who ran it
produces.measured: 2026-11-27: run_by is null in anonymous runs, so a receipt written by the author and one written by a stranger are distinguishable

produces.what: the record of testing someone else's packages with our verifier
produces.measured: 2026-11-27: 58/58 against the shipped kit, and 3/3 against three packages written outside this project
produces.caveat: one person, one machine, one run. Not an audit, not a certification

produces.what: the per-action evidence layout the verifier reads: identity, lifecycle, manifest, evidence files, one digest chain
produces.caveat: documented at the file level, not as a normative specification with a versioned grammar

consumes.measured: 2026-11-27: 58/58 shipped cases, plus 3 foreign packages accepted or refused as their authors expected

2026-11-27: 3 SCITT COSE statements fed straight to our verifier gave 0/3 (S1 and S2 fail, no PASS is invented). Through probityai/agent-evidence-vectors' external rail the same verifier gave 27 vectors executed, 0 passed, 27 failed, 4 suite-level refusals, and the rail named external-output-absent as the cause: our verifier exits 2 and writes no per-vector report line
consumes.blocked_by: no reader for the scitt-cose-carriage-conformance corpus. The output side is no longer the blocker: since 2026-11-27 the verifier can write one report line per package (--report, verify-dir), which is what the external rail named as missing

consumes.measured: 2026-11-27: one cite of RFC 8785 across the 58 cases
2026-11-27: eleven cites of RFC 9162 across the 58 cases

not_claimed: that any of the consumed formats are conformant beyond the cases shipped here
that the verdict vocabulary matches any other project's
that a receipt from this project has been accepted by anyone else
that any third party has reproduced any run of this project
